landmarks.name: Ha Long Bay
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its emerald waters and thousands of towering limestone islands topped with rainforests.

wiki.extract: Hạ Long Bay or Halong Bay is a bay located in Northeastern Vietnam, administered by Quảng Ninh province. The name Hạ Long means "descending dragon". It features thousands of limestone karsts and islets in various shapes and sizes, for which it is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a popular travel destination. The bay is also part of a larger area that includes Bai Tu Long Bay to the northeast and Cát Bà Island to the southwest. These zones share similar geological, geographical, geomorphological, climatic, and cultural characteristics.

landmarks.name: Hue Imperial City
landmarks.writeup: A historic complex of palaces, temples, walls, and gates that was the former imperial capital of Vietnam.

wiki.extract: The Imperial City or Imperial Palace also known as Đại Nội (大內), is a royal enclosure within the walled city of Huế, the former imperial capital of Vietnam during the Nguyễn dynasty. It contains the palaces that housed the imperial family, as well as shrines, gardens, and offices for mandarins. Constructed in 1804 under Emperor Gia Long as a new capital and later re-modelled and enlarged to its current scale in 1833, it mostly served as a ceremonial function and imperial residence during the French colonial period. After the end of the monarchy in 1945, it suffered heavy damage and neglect during the Indochina Wars through the 1980s. The Imperial City was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 as part of the Complex of Huế Monuments and is undergoing restoration.

landmarks.name: My Son Sanctuary
landmarks.writeup: A cluster of abandoned Hindu temples constructed between the 4th and 14th centuries by the Champa civilization.

wiki.extract: Mỹ Sơn is a cluster of abandoned and partially ruined Shaiva Hindu temples in central Vietnam, constructed between the 4th and the 13th century by the Kings of Champa, an Indianized kingdom of the Cham people. The temples are dedicated to the veneration of God in accordance with Shaivism, wherein God is named Shiva, or The Auspicious One. In this particular complex, he is venerated under various local names, the most important of which is Bhadreshvara.

landmarks.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
landmarks.writeup: An extensive network of underground tunnels used by Viet Cong soldiers during the Vietnam War.

wiki.extract: The tunnels of Củ Chi are an immense network of connecting tunnels located in the Củ Chi District of Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam, and are part of a much larger network of tunnels that underlie much of the country. The Củ Chi tunnels were the location of several military campaigns during the Vietnam War, and were the Viet Cong's base of operations for the Tết Offensive in 1968.

landmarks.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
landmarks.writeup: The final resting place of Ho Chi Minh, the revolutionary leader and former president of Vietnam.

wiki.extract: The President Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a mausoleum which serves as the resting place of Vietnamese revolutionary leader and President Ho Chi Minh in Hanoi, Vietnam. It is a large building located in the center of Ba Đình Square, where Ho, Chairman of the Workers' Party of Vietnam from 1951 until his death in 1969, read the Declaration of Independence on September 2, 1945, establishing the Democratic Republic of Vietnam. It is open to the public every morning except Monday and Friday.

cultural_events.name: Tet Nguyen Dan (Lunar New Year)
cultural_events.writeup: The most important celebration marking the arrival of spring and the new lunar year with family reunions and traditional rituals.

wiki.extract: Tết, short for Tết Nguyên Đán, is the most important celebration in Vietnamese culture. Tết celebrates the arrival of spring, which is on the first day of the first Vietnamese lunisolar month, and usually falls between late January and 20 February in the Gregorian calendar.

cultural_events.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A festival celebrating the harvest with lantern parades, mooncakes, and cultural performances.

wiki.extract: The Mid-Autumn Festival, also known as the Moon Festival or Mooncake Festival, is a harvest festival celebrated in Chinese culture. It occurs on the 15th day of the 8th month of the Chinese lunisolar calendar and can fall between 7 September and 8 October (inclusive) of the Gregorian calendar. On this day, the Chinese believe that the moon is at its fullest and brightest, coinciding with the time of harvest in the middle of autumn.

cultural_events.name: Hue Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A biennial cultural event showcasing traditional music, dance, and art in the ancient city of Hue.

wiki.extract: Hue and Cry are a Scottish pop duo formed in 1983 in Coatbridge by the brothers Pat Kane and Greg Kane. The duo are best known for their 1987 single "Labour of Love".

food_writeup: Vietnamese cuisine is known for its balance of five taste elements and fresh ingredients, featuring dishes like pho, banh mi, and spring rolls, emphasizing herbs, rice, and seafood.
brief_history: Vietnam has a history of ancient civilizations, Chinese domination, French colonial rule, and a prolonged struggle for independence culminating in reunification in 1975 under communist leadership.

commentary.inflation_management: The State Bank of Vietnam manages the dong in a crawl against the dollar and has brought inflation down decisively: 23.1% in 2008 and 18.7% in 2011 during the stabilization crisis, then 0.6-4.1% through the late 2010s, 3.2% in 2022, and a projected 3.3% in 2025. The 2011-12 stabilization (tight money, slower credit) was the turning point, establishing credibility that survived the 2022 global shock with only a mild rise. Administered prices (electricity, health) are adjusted in steps, and the central bank has kept the dong's depreciation gradual.
commentary.debt_management: Public debt peaked at 47.9% of GDP in 2016 after the 2011-12 banking crisis cleanup and stimulus, then declined steadily to a projected 30.3% in 2025 on rapid growth (GDP from $84.3bn to a projected $494.1bn) and fiscal restraint. Vietnam is rare in having reduced its debt ratio while growing fast. Borrowing is largely domestic and concessional; the 2022 real-estate and bond-market turmoil (notably the Van Thinh Phat/SCB scandal) created contingent risks but did not reach the sovereign balance sheet. The trajectory is among Asia's healthiest.

Banking crisis and inflation at 18.7%; decisive tightening restored stability.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Vietnam's base case is 6% growth on FDI-led manufacturing, supply-chain diversification from China, and a young workforce, with low inflation and falling debt. Risks are middle-income transition challenges (productivity, skills), the anti-corruption campaign's chilling effect on administration, US tariff exposure given the large bilateral surplus, and climate vulnerability in the Mekong Delta. Analytical assessment: the macro framework is strong; the question is whether governance keeps pace with the economy's ambitions.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
